name: Member_SetItemAtSlot
signature: void Member_SetItemAtSlot(PartyMember* member, int slot, u16 itemId)

params.member: party member; 24 u16 item ids at +0xEC

summary: Writes an item id into inventory slot `slot` of a party member (member+0xEC + slot*2): when the slot is currently equipped it unequips it first through Party_Member_UnequipInventorySlot, then stores the id and, if anything was unequipped, refreshes the derived data (0x00191E3C) and recalculates the member's stats.
evidence: FACTS.md fixes the member inventory as 24 u16 ids at member+0xEC and func_006292A4 as the 'slot is equipped' test, and the body is exactly that: equipped test, unequip, `*(u16*)(member + slot*2 + 0xec) = itemId`, then Party_Member_RecalculateStats. All 13 named callers are inventory operations (Party_Member_EquipInventorySlot, Party_Member_MoveInventoryToBag, Ui_ItemList_RemoveItem, Party_ValidateEquipment...).

name: Member_SwapInventorySlots
signature: u32 Member_SwapInventorySlots(PartyMember* a, int slotA, PartyMember* b, int slotB)
summary: Swaps the item ids in two party-member inventory slots (member+0xEC + slot*2): unequips either slot first when it is equipped, exchanges the two u16 ids, then refreshes both members and recalculates the stats of whichever member had something unequipped. Always returns 1.
evidence: FACTS.md fixes the member inventory at member+0xEC and func_006292A4 as the equipped test; the body reads both slots, unequips the equipped ones, exchanges the two u16 values and calls Party_Member_RecalculateStats on each side. The only caller (maybe_Ui_EquipRow_UpdateCompareText) is an equipment-comparison UI path, which fits a slot swap.
